$comment: S1 cannot be disabled. Note the tier: a failure caused by REVOCATION is on-chain, because Solana enforces it. A failure caused by EXPIRY reports the allowance's stored expiry_tier, which is `signer` under the shipping SPL adapter — invariant I3 does not permit claiming otherwise.

cases.name: pass · an active allowance, well inside its expiry
fail · a revoked allowance is enforced by the chain
fail · a pending allowance has not been read back yet
cases.$why: I4: `active` is a claim about the chain. Before the read-back we do not know the delegation exists, so we do not spend against it.

cases.name: boundary · an expiry exactly equal to now is EXPIRED
cases.$why: `>=`, not `>`. An allowance that expires at 14:00 does not cover a payment at 14:00:00.000.

cases.name: boundary · one millisecond before expiry is still live
fail · a snapshot 61 seconds old fails closed
cases.$why: The specification permits a 60-second cache. A staler view is not evidence that an allowance is live, and failing closed is the safe direction.

cases.name: boundary · a snapshot exactly 60 seconds old is still acceptable
